𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐒𝐓𝐎𝐑𝐘 𝐁𝐄𝐇𝐈𝐍𝐃 𝐅𝐔𝐑𝐈𝐎 𝐆𝐈𝐔𝐍𝐓𝐀⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Before Federico Castelluccio became Furio Giunta on 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐨𝐩𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐨𝐬, acting wasn’t even his original plan. Born in Naples, Italy, he moved to Paterson, New Jersey, with his family when he was three years old. His first passion was art, eventually earning a full scholarship to New York’s School of Visual Arts, where he studied painting and media arts.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Acting came almost by accident. After watching a friend perform a monologue, Castelluccio became fascinated by how completely he transformed into another person. He decided to learn the craft himself, studying acting while performing in theater and taking small roles. But success didn’t come quickly. For years, Castelluccio worked in theater, commercials and television. He had been acting for more than a decade when an opportunity came for a new HBO series called The Sopranos.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
During the first season, Castelluccio actually read for Johnny Sack, a role he immediately felt wasn’t right for him. Months later, his agent called about a new character: Furio Giunta, a gangster from Naples who comes to America to work for Tony Soprano. Suddenly, Castelluccio’s background became a major advantage. He was born in Naples, grew up around Italian-American culture in Paterson and could speak Italian with an authentic Neapolitan accent. He even drew inspiration from his father’s accent and people he knew growing up.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
While Furio eventually disappeared from The Sopranos, Castelluccio continued pursuing his other great passion: painting and collecting art. In 2014, he spotted a painting in Frankfurt listed as an anonymous 18th-century Italian work. Castelluccio suspected it was actually by Guercino, one of the great Italian Baroque painters. He bought it at auction for around $68,000 and invested further in restoration and research. His instinct was right. Experts authenticated it as a genuine Guercino turning his $68,000 discovery into a painting reportedly worth around $10 million.

source_details.title: The Sopranos
source_details.synopsis: The Sopranos is an American crime drama television series created by David Chase for HBO. The series follows Tony Soprano (James Gandolfini), a New Jersey Mafia boss. Suffering from panic attacks, he reluctantly begins seeing psychiatrist Dr. Jennifer Melfi (Lorraine Bracco), who encourages him to open up about his difficulties balancing his family life with his criminal activities. Other important characters include Tony's family, Mafia colleagues, and rivals, most notably his wife Carmela (Edie Falco), his nephew and protégé Christopher Moltisanti (Michael Imperioli), and his uncle Corrado "Junior" Soprano (Dominic Chianese). Greenlit in 1997, the series was broadcast on HBO from January 1
